title: Rules for thinking errors, pointers for facts
statement: When a wrong answer comes from a kind of thinking, give a transferable rule that separates right from wrong; point back to the text only for a missed fact.
detail: A grade-3 reading rulebook requires every wrong-answer reply to name the misconception in the child's own terms, give a way forward and stop short of the answer. The way forward is a criterion when the error is a kind of thinking and a text pointer only when it is a missed fact, because a criterion transfers to the next item and a page reference does not. Its validator holds a reply that is missing, under 6 words, states the answer, shares 6 words in a row with the correct option or repeats the correct-answer reply, and warns above 45 words, none of which tells a criterion from a pointer.
against: The rule leaves its central judgment to people: "Whether the named misconception is actually right stays a review job." (`grade3-reading/artifacts/judgment-corpus/distilled-src/07-SCORING-FEEDBACK-XP.md`, line 119). The record feedback-that-sends-the-student-back has feedback on a wrong answer say where to look, which this rule keeps for missed facts only.

evidence.quote: **Every wrong-answer reply does exactly three things (R-Q-22)**: names the misconception in the child's own terms, gives a way forward, and stops short of the answer

The way forward is a criterion (a transferable rule) when the error is a kind of thinking, and a text pointer only when the error is a missed fact; a criterion transfers to the next item, a page reference does not.
missing reply, <6 words, states answer, 6-word verbatim overlap with the correct option, identical to the correct-answer reply; warns >45 words.
**Rule.** Every wrong-answer reply does three things and no more.
Either point at where the text settles it ("Look at the sentences about learning an epic by ear") or hand over the criterion that separates right from wrong here ("A reason comes before the action").
A criterion is the better hint of the two when the child's error is about a kind of thinking rather than a missed fact, because it transfers to the next item and a page reference does not.
vocabulary misses need conceptual correction rather than a passage redirect.
